govdocs-archive_org-lifschultz-1979-bang: Lawrence Lifschultz’s Bangladesh: The Unfinished Revolution — 1979 — reports on the young nation’s turmoil. The journalist’s pages cover coups, famine, and murder. Mujib’s assassination shadows the tale. The reporting is first-hand. The book is a landmark of South Asian reportage.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AssassinationJF: Mike Cochran’s Associated Press piece — Kennedy Mystique and Conspiracy Theories Thrive — marks 25 years after Dallas. The wire story surveyed the enduring JFK fascination. The piece belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CouncilorThe_Co: This item — The Councilor — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. The title suggests a political pamphlet. The file may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CubaProjectThe_: This item — Book Publishing Announcements, Cuba Project Fragment, creator unknown — is a publishing file. The file’s full context is unclear. The Cuba Project was the CIA’s anti-Castro program. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of publishing history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DefenderThe_Def: Gerald B. Winrod’s Defender, Vol. 18, No. 5 — September 1943 — is an issue of the far-right paper. Winrod’s paper spread hate in the war years. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ProgressiveThe_: This letter to Erwin Knoll of The Progressive — December 24, creator unknown — is a press note. The Progressive was the dissenters’ magazine. The letter may hold a clue. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
dick-prescott-s-first-year-at-west-point: H. Irving Hancock launches his West Point series with Dick Prescott and his chum beginning cadet life at the famous military academy. Drill, discipline, hazing, and schoolboy honor fill their first year in cadet gray. Written for boys who dreamed of the academy, the story celebrates pluck, loyalty, and the making of young officers.
the-story-of-rome-from-the-earliest-time: Arthur Gilman retells the rise of Rome for young readers, from Romulus and Remus through the fall of the Republic. Kings, consuls, and conquerors march through clear, lively chapters that make ancient history feel like adventure. Written for schools and families, it has introduced generations of children to the glory and drama of ancient Rome.
myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-volume: This volume follows the Delaware River through tales of colonial settlers, Lenni Lenape legends, and Revolutionary ghosts. Skinner collected his stories from newspapers, histories, and local tellers, giving each a storyteller's polish. The result is a treasury of mid-Atlantic folklore, eerie and charming by turns.
a-popular-history-of-ireland-from-the-ea: Irish patriot Thomas D'Arcy McGee tells his country's story from ancient times to Catholic Emancipation with passion and pride. Kings and saints, invasions and rebellions fill a narrative written by a man who loved Ireland deeply. Long a standard popular history, it carries the fire of a true Irish nationalist.
the-treaties-of-canada-with-the-indians-: Alexander Morris, who made the treaties himself, records Canada's bargains with the Indians of Manitoba and the Northwest — the numbered treaties that opened the West. An official, firsthand record of fateful agreements. Essential Canadian history. Morris himself smoked the peace pipe and signed the papers that shaped the West.
the-motor-girls-on-waters-blue-or-the-st: Margaret Penrose sends her Motor Girls on waters blue — a strange cruise aboard the Tartar full of mystery and fun. The girls' pluck and friendship carry them through. Another bright adventure for series readers. Island mysteries and nautical fun keep the Motor Girls busy from port to port.
grisly-grisell-or-the-laidly-lady-of-whi: Charlotte Yonge's historical tale follows Grisly Grisell, the laidly lady of Whitburn, through the Wars of the Roses — disfigurement, devotion, and a strange, touching love. Her story unfolds against England's bloodiest family feud, lit by Yonge's deep sympathy. A moving romance from a beloved Victorian novelist.
psyche: Molière's Psyche — his gorgeous court spectacle on the myth of Cupid and Psyche — dazzled Louis XIV's court with music, dance, and poetry combined. The playwright as royal showman at his most baroque and splendid. A glittering piece of theater history.
through-central-borneo-an-account-of-two: Carl Lumholtz spent two years in the land of head-hunters — through central Borneo, among the Dayaks — and lived to write this thrilling account. His explorations opened unknown jungles to science. A classic of travel and anthropology. His photographs and notes remain a treasure of ethnology.
the-outdoor-girls-in-army-service-or-doi: Laura Lee Hope's Outdoor Girls do army service — doing their bit for the soldier boys of the Great War. The series heroines serve with pluck, kindness, and good cheer. A patriotic favorite of wartime girl readers everywhere. Betty, Mollie, Amy, and Grace serve with smiles and courage.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-absinthe: A 1913 entry on absinthe — the bitter wormwood of Scripture. Anthony Maas traces its biblical mentions. Bitterness and judgment gather round the herb. A short note on a somber plant. The star called Wormwood falls in the Apocalypse. Its bitterness suited the prophets' warnings.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alanus-de-rup: A 1913 entry on Alanus de Rupe — Alan de la Roche, the Dominican apostle of the Rosary. John McNicholas tells his mission. He preached Mary's beads across the north. Confraternities sprang from his word. The Rosary's great reviver. His visions renewed the Marian devotion.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexandre-ant: A 1913 entry on Archbishop Taché — the apostle of the Canadian northwest. Adrian Morice honors his missionary zeal. St. Boniface became his see. He served Indians and settlers alike. Manitoba's great churchman. His cathedral crowns the Red River. His missions spanned the frozen prairies.
